about: What one `aside repl` run prints and how it is read (appendix A 8), in the protocol the skill's Aside unit will speak (ported in P3 from the facebook skill's aside/program.js): zero or more {"kind":"chunk","index":i,"body"} lines, then one {"kind":"result","chunks":n,"body"} line, or one {"kind":"error","error"} line. Each case gives the process result (stdout, stderr, exit; timed_out when it did not finish) and the outcome: value (what the page function returned) or error with its kind: invalid, tab_missing, lost (time limit or lost connection), failed (other nonzero exit), timeout. The previous reader's body_file refusal has no counterpart: in this protocol a result never names a file, so a run that does not end in one result or error line is invalid.

cases.name: plain-result
cases.fact: The last line is the result; its body is the JSON of what the page function returned.

cases.name: ansi-and-noise-lines
cases.fact: ANSI colour codes are stripped and only lines starting with { are JSON; Aside status lines and update notices are noise.
cases.stdout:
[33mAside CLI 9.9 is available[0m
✔︎ Opened a tab
[32m{"kind": "result", "chunks": 0, "body": "[1,2]"}[0m
[2m[ok | 12ms][0m

cases.name: line-separator-inside-text
cases.fact: Post text can hold U+2028, U+2029 or U+0085, which JSON.stringify leaves literal: only a newline ends a line, so the result is read whole.

cases.name: chunked-result
cases.fact: A large result arrives as chunk lines in index order before a result line whose chunks equals their count.

cases.name: chunk-count-mismatch
cases.fact: chunks must equal the number of chunk lines.

cases.name: chunk-order-mismatch
cases.fact: Chunk indexes must run 0, 1, 2 ... in order.

cases.name: two-results
cases.fact: Exactly one result line ends a run.

cases.name: no-json
cases.fact: No JSON line at all is an invalid response.

cases.name: tab-missing
cases.fact: A tab that no longer exists is reported so the caller can reopen it.

cases.name: evaluate-failed
cases.fact: A page function that threw is an Aside failure, not a Threads answer.

cases.name: other-side-closed
cases.fact: A nonzero exit mentioning 'other side closed' is the REPL time limit or a lost connection.

cases.name: daemon-unreachable
cases.fact: A nonzero exit mentioning 'daemon is not reachable' is a lost connection.

cases.name: other-nonzero-exit
cases.fact: Any other nonzero exit is a failed Aside call.
cases.stderr: TypeError: x is not a function

cases.name: process-timeout
cases.fact: A run that does not finish within the process limit (the REPL's 120 s plus 5) is stopped and reported as a timeout; the request may have been made.
